column2: a website looks almost like a real one but the address is misspelled
column3: check the address carefully, like "amaz0n" instead of "amazon"
column4: fake sites copy real ones with tiny spelling changes

column2: a shocking headline in big capital letters
column3: read beyond the headline and check other sources
column4: headlines are written to make you click and can be misleading

column2: a story comes from a funny news website like The Onion
column3: know some sites write satire: made-up news as jokes
column4: satire is not lying when readers know it is a joke, but it can fool people who don't

column2: an account posts many messages repeating the same thing
column3: know some accounts are bots or fake accounts
column4: they make an idea look more popular than it is

column2: a friend pressures you into skipping a lesson
column4: it gets you in trouble and worries school staff who must know where you are

column2: you find out a family secret, like a present for Christmas
column4: spoiling a present takes the joy from the giver

column2: you lied before and your parents check up on you more now
column3: keep telling the truth and trust will grow back slowly
column4: trust is quick to lose and slow to rebuild

column2: a teacher leaves the class for a moment
column3: behave as if they were there
column4: being good when no one is watching is what makes you trustworthy
